international.title: Federal court clears way for army to detonate bomb-making material in Iowa
international.summary: Decision comes after Trump urged court to first sign off on what he called the safest way to resolve the situation The US army can proceed with detonating several tons of degraded bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, a federal appeals court ruled on Monday. The order came after a day of uncertainty that saw Donald Trump attempt to foist responsibility “for any and all death or destruction” on Iowa’s Democratic governor-elect Rob Sands. The detonation of 68 barrels containing nearly 9,500lb of lead azide was initially planned for Friday, but the army has since changed the date three times after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
